sections.html:
Buena Vista County sits in northwest Iowa with Storm Lake as seat and largest city. The 2020 count was 20,823 people, and Storm Lake alone had 11,269 of them. Alta follows with 2,087, then a string of small towns from Newell (906) down to Truesdale (69).

Lakeside, on the east shore of Storm Lake, is its own small city, separate from Storm Lake itself. If your address is by the water, check the parcel record to see which city it falls in, since that affects which levies appear on the bill.

The treasurer collects and the assessor values. Both are at 215 E. 5th Street in Storm Lake, with windows open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Buena Vista County property tax offices
OfficePhoneMailing address
Treasurer712-749-2533P.O. Drawer 149, Storm Lake, IA 50588
Assessor712-749-2543P.O. Box 148, Storm Lake, IA 50588

The property tax window is on the first floor of the courthouse. You can pay at iowatreasurers.org, by mail, in the secure drop box on the courthouse's east side, or in person.

Buena Vista County bills in two halves. The first is due on or before September 30, and the second runs from March 1 through March 31. Once a half goes late, a penalty of 1.5 percent per month begins, starting October 1 for the fall half. A postmark dated by the deadline counts as on time, and online payments are accepted until 11:59 p.m. that day. When a deadline lands on a weekend, it moves to the next business day.

Enclose the payment stubs from your statement so the money is applied to the right parcel.

  • August: statements are mailed.
  • September 30: first half deadline.
  • March 31: second half deadline.
  • June: annual tax sale of delinquent parcels.

The assessor revalues real property every two years, in odd-numbered years, as of January 1. Informal review runs April 2 to April 25, and a formal protest to the Board of Review runs April 2 to April 30. In odd years, appeals of an equalization order can be filed October 9 to 31.

The board meets from May 1 until it adjourns. Its members include a farmer, a real estate agent and someone with building knowledge. If the board's decision leaves you unsatisfied, the next steps are the Property Assessment Appeal Board or district court. A disaster proclamation can stretch these windows to May 25 and June 5.

Starting with assessment year 2026, the homestead credit became a homestead exemption. It equals 10 percent of the home's taxable value, with a minimum of $5,500 and a maximum of $20,000, and the claim is due by July 1. Those with military service may also qualify for a $4,000 military exemption. The assessor handles both, so call 712-749-2543 if you are unsure what is on your parcel.

A buyer should plan to file a claim of their own after closing, ideally before July 1 so the benefit starts on the next bill.

sections.h2: Unpaid taxes and the June tax sale
sections.html:
Parcels with unpaid tax go to a yearly auction at the courthouse each June, and all bids are placed online. Redemption cannot be handled through the website. Call 712-749-2533 or visit the treasurer.

To redeem, an owner pays the delinquent tax plus 2 percent for every month since the sale. Each year the county posts a delinquent tax list, along with a notice to tax sale purchasers. Looking at that list before you put a house on the market shows whether the parcel is already lined up for the June sale, and the treasurer can give a payoff figure for a specific closing date.

Iowa's transfer tax comes to 80 cents on each $500 of value above $500, and the seller is the person liable. The county recorder collects it, and a declaration of value is submitted when the deed is recorded. Iowa Code section 428A.2 exempts some transfers, among them gifts between spouses or between parent and child and distributions to heirs without consideration.

If you own a house in Storm Lake, Alta or a smaller town and the taxes or repairs have piled up, a cash sale as-is is one way to close without a listing.

Start with the treasurer. Ask for a payoff that covers both halves and any penalty accrued to your expected closing date, and check the posted delinquent list to be sure your parcel is not on it. Next, contact the assessor about the homestead exemption and any military exemption, because a buyer will want to know what stays and what must be refiled. Then gather the deed so the declaration of value can go in at recording. Once these pieces are collected, the title company can set the closing, deduct the tax from your proceeds, and send the deed to the recorder. Pay attention to your own calendar too: a sale that closes in late spring or summer may fall before the first July 1 claim deadline, which gives the new owner time to file for the exemption.

sections.h2: Walking through a sale with taxes owed
sections.html:
Picture a Storm Lake owner who fell behind on the fall half. Interest has been building since October 1, and if the parcel reaches the June auction it lands on the delinquent list. At that stage the number to learn is the redemption amount, which is the tax sold plus the monthly charge. Ask the treasurer for it in writing with a date the figure stays good, hand it to the title company, and let the closing pay it from your proceeds. Nothing about this blocks a sale. It only adds a line to the settlement statement.

If the parcel has not been sold, the process is shorter: confirm the balance, pay it at closing, and keep the receipt.

sections.h2: Questions to put to the assessor
sections.html: Call 712-749-2543 and ask which exemptions are on file. Ask whether your parcel is in a reassessment year, because values are reset every two years and a buyer may ask what is coming. Ask when informal review opens, since a short talk in April may settle a disagreement before it needs a formal protest. If the property sits near the lake, ask which city levies apply, and make sure the address on the bill matches the parcel record.

faqs.q: When are Buena Vista County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due by September 30 and the second half by March 31. Late payments carry a penalty of 1.5 percent per month.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Buena Vista County property tax?
faqs.a: At the property tax window on the first floor of the courthouse, 215 E. 5th Street, Storm Lake. You can also pay at iowatreasurers.org, by mail, or in the drop box on the courthouse's east side.

faqs.q: How often does Buena Vista County reassess property?
faqs.a: Every two years, in odd-numbered years, as of January 1.

faqs.q: When can I protest my Buena Vista County assessment?
faqs.a: A formal protest to the Board of Review can be filed April 2 to April 30. Informal review runs April 2 to April 25.

faqs.q: Can I redeem a property after the tax sale?
faqs.a: Yes, within the time Iowa law allows. Call the treasurer at 712-749-2533 or visit in person, because redemption cannot be paid through the website.
